title: PB1.4 - 70 Gerrard Street East - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act

stages.body: Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning
stages.summary:
This report recommends that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 70 Gerrard
Street East under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value according
to the Statement of Significance which includes a description of heritage attributes found in Attachment
1.
 
The subject property at 70 Gerrard Street East is located on the north side of Gerrard Street East, at
the northeast corner of Church Street, within the Downtown Yonge East neighbourhood of downtown
Toronto.
 
A location map and current photograph of the heritage property are included in Attachment 2.
 
Constructed c. 1845 and substantially altered in 1886 according to plans by Langley & Burke, the
property historically known as the Dr. James Elliot Graham House contains a remodelled Queen Anne
Revival style, two-and-a-half-storey detached house-form building, which was originally designed in the
Georgian style. Following its long tenure as a private residence, the subject property has since the
1970s been home to a series of commercial and institutional establishments and organizations,
including Egerton's Restaurant, The Edge music venue, and Under 21/Covenant House. The property
forms part of a group of surviving mid- to late-19-century house-form buildings around the intersection
of Church Street and Gerrard Street East, in the east section of downtown Toronto.
 
The subject property at 70 Gerrard Street East was listed on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register on
March 15, 1974.
 
This property is one of eighteen pre-1870 listed properties citywide which have been identified as
candidates for designation through the City's implementation of Bill 23 amendments to the Ontario
Heritage Act and its ongoing prioritization strategy for listed properties that must be designated or
removed from the Heritage Register by January 1, 2027.

stages.recommendations:
The Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning recommends that:
 
1. City Council state its intention to designate the property at 70 Gerrard Street East under Part IV,
Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act in accordance with the Statement of Significance for 70 Gerrard
Street East (Reasons for Designation) attached as Attachment 1, to the report, October 28, 2026, from
the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning.
 
2. If there are no objections to the designation, City Council authorize the City Solicitor to introduce the
Bill in Council designating the property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act.
